own_solution.law: Steady radial conduction in a cylindrical shell with constant k: T(r) = T1 - (T1-T2) ln(r/r1)/ln(r2/r1); drop to r is (T1-T2) ln(r/r1)/ln(r2/r1)
assumptions: surface temperatures fixed at 420 K (r=3 cm) and 300 K (r=9 cm)

defect_reasons.other: With T21B1/T15F5 the base text still says 'the outer surface of the insulation is held at 300 K'; the intended reading (new outer surface at 10.8 cm held at 300 K, the 9 cm surface no longer clamped) is the natural one but the wording could be read as the 9 cm surface still being held at 300 K, which would leave the answer at 55.80 K.

notes: Base: 120*ln(5/3)/ln(3) = 120*0.51083/1.09861 = 55.797 K. With the extra 1.8 cm (outer radius 10.8 cm at 300 K): 120*ln(5/3)/ln(3.6) = 120*0.51083/1.28093 = 47.855 K. Conductivity cancels. 'Earlier survey only' sentences refer to a past configuration and the tank sentences to a separate object: disconnected. Variant pairs: T2495/T8870 same 0.07 W/(m*K); T6641/T21B1/T15F5/T8754 all 1.8 cm; T26FA/T6E73 both 'small thickness' (no number). T21B1 wording 'While the heat flows steadily, the layer is wrapped' is slightly awkward.
